title: Informing for Equity: A Systemic Framework for GenAI Assessment in Resource-Constrained Higher Education
venue: Informing Science: The International Journal of an Emerging Transdiscipline
extended_summary:
The paper addresses how generative AI may deepen inequities in resource-constrained higher education, especially where institutions face unreliable connectivity, limited device access, linguistic barriers, and weak policy guidance. It frames the problem not as isolated issues of access, pedagogy, or ethics, but as an institutional “informing systems” failure in which students, faculty, and administrators receive inconsistent or inadequate guidance about acceptable and meaningful GenAI use.

Rather than evaluating a specific classroom intervention, the paper develops a Systemic Framework for Equitable GenAI Assessment through a systematic literature synthesis of 47 sources, grounded in critical pedagogy, digital equity theory, and institutional theory. The framework has three interlocking principles: infrastructure-based equity, transparent collaboration, and institutional scaffolding. These are intended to support equitable access, process-oriented AI-integrated assessment, and institution-level governance and training.

The context is resource-constrained higher education, with Philippine higher education used as an illustrative paradigmatic case. The framework considers multiple stakeholder groups, including students, faculty, administrators, and institutions, and emphasizes Global South settings where AI adoption is shaped by infrastructure gaps and colonial or linguistic inequities.

The main conclusion is that fragmented responses—such as buying AI detectors, offering one-off workshops, or changing assignments without ensuring student access—are likely to fail because infrastructural exclusion, pedagogical misalignment, and ethical displacement reinforce one another. The paper argues for phased but integrated implementation, beginning with institutional scaffolding and small-scale pilots that coordinate access support, assessment redesign, and policy development. The model is explicitly presented as theoretically grounded but not yet empirically validated.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI systems, including large language models, capable of producing text and supporting AI-human interaction in educational work and assessment contexts.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper examines GenAI as a systemic disruption to higher education assessment in resource-constrained institutions and proposes a Systemic Framework for Equitable GenAI Assessment addressing infrastructure equity, transparent collaboration, and institutional scaffolding.

quality_tier_rationale: The study uses a systematic literature synthesis of 47 sources with stated search/selection procedures and thematic synthesis, but it is conceptual and not an empirical evaluation, RCT, QED, or meta-analysis of outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not report empirical effectiveness or student outcome impacts for a GenAI tool; it proposes a conceptual/systemic framework based on literature synthesis. Therefore impact is unclear rather than demonstrated.
